title: Island hopping to Guam and the whiskey ban for enlisted men
summary: They refuel on Johnston Island, Kwajalein and Guam, where a G.I. says enlisted men cannot buy a drink, so Pillars shares a bottle with him.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Were you playing when you stopped in Guam and Manila?
No, no, no. We stopped to refuel and eat.
We left Honolulu and -- Wake Island?
No, we didn't go to Wake, no.
MR. PILLARS: Johnson Island, Kwajalein, and Guam. Now, Kwajalein is where that experimented with that atomic bomb, remember? Kwajalein Island. With those islands, you could --

MR. PILLARS: When you would fly over it, it looked just like this bed here, it had water all around it, see. Sometimes the plane would hit just a few feet in the water, it wasn't deep water, you know what I mean. It would hit that water and then hit the runway, see, and then it would just barely stop before going --

Over the other end into water, you know what I mean, see. And we would get off and we would stop and get a little bite to eat, and they usually had Navy personnel there, and the personnel -- they -- everybody was mad as a wolf, because you're out there, you can't communicate with nobody, you know what I mean, nowhere to go. And, boy, everybody was mean mad at you. And we got to Guam, I ran into a G.I., was sitting out there on some rocks, right by the water. He was shaking his head. I said, 'What do you say was there, partner, how you doing?' He says, 'Man, it's not human.' I said, 'What's wrong?' He said, 'We just got through unloading almost a shipload of whisky. And do you know, an enlisted man is not allowed -- he can't buy a drink of whisky on this island.' I said, 'You've got to be kidding.' He says, 'My hand to God. I went back in the airport, because he was waiting, see. And reached in the bag and got a bottle of Sunnybrook whisky. And I went back out there -- I don't know who else was with me, but somebody else in the band, either one of the show fellows, and we sat down and opened that whisky and the boy said, 'Oh, my, my, my. Oh, my.' And I took a drink out of the thing, and my friend took a drink, and then I gave it to him. I said, 'Man, help yourself, man.' So, boy, that guy was just so happy, he was just so happy.
So we had another drink out of it, and I gave the rest of it and said, 'Take it all and give it to some of your friends.'

And gave it to him. When I heard that -- see, I had heard about Guam. Guam is controlled by the Navy and that was one of those things. I guess that's the way they did it, back during that time. But it's different now.
